author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Qualcomm: China Boost - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM)
text:
According to published news reports, Qualcomm ( QCOM ) shareholders are about to get the long awaited EPS boost via the NXP Semiconductor ( NXPI ) merger. Investors that held through the pain and took advantage of the recent stock dip to $50 are about to get rewarded. The next step is for Qualcomm to reach $70.
Source: NXP Semi. website
China Regulators The combination of Qualcomm and NXP Semi. never had cause for regulator concern. The businesses doesn't overlap and for this reason all regulators approved the deal but China that only seemed to want assurances on licensing limits for mobile payments and autonomous driving.
The escalating trade wars with China made the deal a potential casualty of trade tensions. China blocked the deal back in November, but the news over the holiday weekend suggests the merger is about to get approved. According to Bloomberg , senior officials have already given approval for the deal. The only hold-up now is the ZTE Corp. ( OTC:ZTCOY ) ban.
After banning the large Chinese telecom in April from buying U.S. technology components due to violating sanctions against Iran and North Korea, a possible resolution and fine would go along way for China approving the Qualcomm and NXP Semi. merger. ZTE has virtually shut down causing embarrassment to China and the potential loss of thousands of jobs.
Reuters quoted a source in the deal:
It feels as though it's getting close to the end.
The deal could still fall apart, but both countries now have bargaining chips on the table. Most importantly though, China needs to restart operations at ZTE and standing in the way of the Qualcomm/NXP Semi deal for no viable reason doesn't help their cause.
Next Stop: $70 My investment thesis going back for months now was that Qualcomm needed to come to a conclusion on the deal one way or another day. Even canceling the deal provided tremendous upside for the stock as the company has the ability to boost EPS either way.
Based on current analyst estimates of Qualcomm earning under $4 per share next year, analysts aren't accurately factoring in either prescribed outcome for FY19.
QCOM EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts
For this reason, the wireless tech giant recently announced a $10 billion share repurchase plan . The announcement came when the stock was trading around $53 and a friendly reminder to the market that Qualcomm can easily boost EPS estimates with or without NXP Semi.
Back along with the blocking of the Broadcom ( AVGO ) attempted buyout, Qualcomm provided a logical path to earning $5.25 per share. Either the company closes the accretive NXP Semi deal or spends $25 billion on stock repurchases that both provide $1.50 accretion to EPS.
Source: Qualcomm FQ2'18 presentation
Either way, Qualcomm has a verified path to a significant EPS boost. The above analyst EPS estimates only factor in the $1 billion cost savings plan to reach the $3.80 target in FY19. So the actual path and specific timing is unknown causing a known EPS boost to be ignored by analysts.
The issue is more regarding timing on whether the full $1.50 accretive earnings are achieved in FY19 that starts in October. A deal with NXP Semi. that closes in June or July might not have time to fully realize the $500 million synergies by the start of the year and the large stock buyback might not be complete even by year end.
Either way, Qualcomm has the potential for pro-forma earnings of $5.25. Even using a more conservative EPS target of $5 for next year, the stock only trades at 12x EPS estimates. A more logical 14x target brings the stock up to $70.
This analysis excludes a further boost to EPS targets of closing the royalty deals with Apple ( AAPL ) and Huawei . Qualcomm has estimated another $2 per share boost from closing these deals that are more about terms of royalty amounts rather than whether these smartphone companies will or won't pay.
These royalty deals are again known unknowns. Nobody knows the specifics of the deals including the timing, but everybody knows that Qualcomm will eventually reclaim royalty payments from Apple at likely reduced terms.
The stock ultimately has upside to $100 on these known events, but Qualcomm will initially only trade up to $70 as Apple isn't likely to close anytime soon. For this reason, the company logically blocked the initial Broadcom deal at $81 and the former Chairman wanted to take the company private.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that China is likely to approve the NXP Semi. deal in order to find a working solution for ZTE. The ability for Qualcomm to finally take the next step on one of the EPS boosting options that will boost EPS to over $5 will provide the next leg for the stock heading higher.
